## gitmoot

```text
gitmoot coordinates local AI agent sessions through GitHub PRs.

Usage:
  gitmoot <command> [flags]

Commands:
  init       initialize local Gitmoot state
  doctor     check local Gitmoot prerequisites
  version    show Gitmoot version and build metadata
  config     show local Gitmoot config paths
  org        org registry, attribution, and brief/chart/status (RFC #1042)
  message    send, read and reply to durable fleet messages
  key        manage keycard registry metadata
  update     check for and apply Gitmoot releases
  setup      register a repo and initial reviewer
  repo       manage watched repositories
  daemon     run the local PR watcher
  reviewer   manage registered reviewers
  ask        ask a registered reviewer a read-only question
  review     request a routed independent review and follow its verdict
  runtime    inspect runtime metadata (models, capabilities, usage)
  sandbox    probe kernel-enforced runtime sandbox support
  plugin     build and inspect Gitmoot agent plugins
  status     show local reviewer, pr and run counts
  pr         inspect pull requests and their review state
  run        inspect and recover runs (reviews, asks, implementation records)
  findings   report the review findings ledger per repository
  workflow   inspect external-coordinator workflow groups and notes
  dashboard  show a snapshot of local Gitmoot state
```

## gitmoot ask

```text
Usage:
  gitmoot ask <reviewer> "question" [--repo owner/repo] [--background] [--action ask] [--model model] [--effort effort] [--campaign label] [--org-role role] [--runtime rt] [--session ref] [--home path] [--json] [--force]
  --runtime omp|shell runs THIS run on the named runtime; the reviewer's registered default runtime is unchanged.
    The overridden run never resumes the reviewer's default-runtime session: it runs on a fresh session of the
    override runtime, or on --session <ref> (an explicit session id, or — required for shell — a command;
    "last" is rejected because it resumes whichever session is most recent).
    Model rule: --model with --runtime is interpreted for the OVERRIDE runtime; without --model the run uses the
    override runtime's default model (the reviewer's configured default model is never applied to another runtime).
    Effort rule: --effort with --runtime is interpreted for the OVERRIDE runtime; without --effort the run uses the
    override runtime's default effort (the reviewer's configured default effort is never applied to another runtime).
```

## gitmoot daemon

```text
Usage:
  gitmoot daemon start [--repo owner/repo] [--poll 30s] [--workers 1 | --parallel N] [--scheduler barrier|pool] [--watch-issues]
  gitmoot daemon run [--repo owner/repo] [--poll 30s] [--workers 1 | --parallel N] [--scheduler barrier|pool] [--watch-issues]
  gitmoot daemon stop
  gitmoot daemon restart
  gitmoot daemon status
  gitmoot daemon drain [--timeout 15m] [--clear]
  gitmoot daemon logs

  --repo owner/repo SCOPES the daemon to a SINGLE repo: it polls only that repo's PRs and
  claims only that repo's queued jobs. Omit --repo to supervise ALL enabled registered repos.
```

## gitmoot daemon restart

```text
Usage of daemon restart:
  -home string
    	home directory to use instead of the current user's home
  -parallel int
    	run jobs in parallel: sets --workers N and --scheduler pool together (#444)
  -poll duration
    	poll interval (default 30s)
  -repo string
    	GitHub repository as owner/repo: scopes the daemon to a SINGLE repo (polls only that repo's PRs; claims only that repo's queued jobs). Omit to supervise ALL enabled registered repos
  -root string
    	alias for --session
  -scheduler string
    	queued-job scheduler: barrier (default) or pool (#394 opt-in continuous worker pool) (default "barrier")
  -session string
    	scope the daemon worker to one job id (and jobs whose payload names it as root_job_id)
  -watch-issues
    	poll open issues and route @<reviewer> ask comments to jobs (#389)
  -workers int
    	worker count (default 1)
```

## gitmoot message

```text
Usage:
  gitmoot message send ROLE "TEXT" [--workflow LABEL] [--role ROLE] [--json] [--home DIR]
  gitmoot message inbox [--before ID] [--limit 20] [--role ROLE] [--json] [--home DIR]
  gitmoot message show ID [--thread] [--before ID] [--limit 20] [--role ROLE] [--json] [--home DIR]
  gitmoot message reply ID "TEXT" [--role ROLE] [--json] [--home DIR]
  gitmoot message escalate [--workflow LABEL] [--to ROLE] [--repo OWNER/REPO] [--role ROLE] [--json] [--home DIR] "QUESTION"
  gitmoot message resolve ID [--answer TEXT | --note ID] [--role ROLE] [--json] [--home DIR]
  gitmoot message pending --claim --hook UserPromptSubmit|PostToolUse|Stop --runtime claude|codex
  gitmoot message directive send|ack|done|cancel --help

Messages are durable ordinary conversation between registered fleet roles.
No workflow, job, subscription or acknowledgment is required. Flags follow positional arguments.
-h, -help or --help anywhere prints usage and saves nothing.
Message text that is a single flag-like word, such as --help or -x, is refused.
Sender defaults to GITMOOT_ORG_ROLE, then the current registered Herdr pane.
--role is an operator attribution override, not an authentication credential.
Saved mail, notification submission, reading and task completion are separate facts.
Escalations track decisions; directives retain issuer and recipient authority checks.
```

## gitmoot message directive

```text
Usage:
  gitmoot message directive send --to ROLE [--workflow LABEL] [--role ROLE] [--json] [--home DIR] (--stdin | -F FILE | TEXT)
  gitmoot message directive ack ID [--role ROLE] [--json] [--home DIR]
  gitmoot message directive cancel ID [--role ROLE] [--json] [--home DIR]
  gitmoot message directive done ID [--role ROLE] [--json] [--home DIR]
Acknowledgment records receipt and is open to the target or an ancestor.
`done` records COMPLETION and ends the obligation, including its TTL nudges;
it is restricted to the TARGET SUBTREE -- the addressed role or one below it.
Ancestors cannot complete (a sender is always an ancestor, so that would be
self-certification); they may cancel instead. Only the sender may cancel.
-h, -help or --help prints this usage and saves nothing. A TEXT body that is a
single flag-like word, such as -x, is refused; put -- before it to send it anyway.
```

## gitmoot message pending

```text
Usage: gitmoot message pending --claim --hook UserPromptSubmit|PostToolUse|Stop --runtime claude|codex [--role ROLE] [--home DIR]

Claims the acting role's pending inbox notifications for a Claude Code or Codex
turn hook, marks them submitted with a turn-hook receipt, and prints that
runtime's hook JSON naming each message once. No pending mail prints nothing.
The command always exits 0 so a hook never fails the agent's turn; problems are
reported on stderr only.
```

## gitmoot org await

```text
Usage:
  gitmoot org await review --repo OWNER/REPO --pr NUMBER --head SHA --ttl DURATION [--role ROLE] [--home DIR]
  gitmoot org await list [--role ROLE] [--state waiting|satisfied|expired|superseded] [--json] [--home DIR]
  gitmoot org await withdraw [--role ROLE] --reason TEXT [--home DIR] ID
Every awaited fact has a required deadline. A matching exact-head review verdict satisfies it. At the deadline a review wait the PR has moved past (a later wait on another head, merged, closed, or a new head) ends superseded with its reason and wakes nobody; any other wait expires, remains queryable, and wakes the waiter (an archived waiter's nearest live ancestor). The waiter may withdraw a waiting fact it no longer needs (for example after cancelling the review on purpose): it ends superseded as "withdrawn by ROLE: REASON" and wakes nobody.
```

## gitmoot review

```text
Usage:
  gitmoot review request --pr NUMBER [--repo OWNER/REPO] [--head SHA] [--branch NAME] [--purpose code|security|ui|architecture] [--role ROLE] [--ttl DURATION] [--reviewer NAME] [--message TEXT] [--runtime NAME] [--exec-backend local|remote] [--exec-provider e2b|sandboxd|sandboxd-linux] [--model PROVIDER/MODEL] [--effort LEVEL] [--campaign LABEL] [--session REF] [--full] [--post-merge] [--no-execution] [--part NAME [--supersede RUN --reason TEXT]] [--related-pr N]... [--allow-prompt-head-mismatch] [--background] [--json] [--home DIR] [-- "review instructions"]
  gitmoot review status --pr NUMBER [--repo OWNER/REPO] [--json] [--home DIR]
  gitmoot review level --repo OWNER/REPO --pr NUMBER [--json] [--home DIR]
  gitmoot review list [--repo owner/repo] [--state state] [--workflow label] [--json]
  gitmoot review show <id> [--json]
  gitmoot review watch <id> [--poll 1s] [--json] [--transcript [--log-path path] [--runtime runtime]]
  gitmoot review cancel <id>

request routes one independent review of the pull request's current (or --head) commit.
Gitmoot picks a review-capable reviewer (or --reviewer), runs it on omp with the [review_router] model pool
for the purpose, falls back to the next model on a provider quota/auth failure, and
wakes --role (default $GITMOOT_ORG_ROLE) when the verdict is saved. A second request for
the same head attaches to the running review or to its saved verdict; it never spends
another reviewer. No verdict ever triggers a model change.
```

## gitmoot review request

```text
Usage of review request:
  -allow-prompt-head-mismatch
    	dispatch even when a carried finding cites a commit outside this pull request's history
  -background
    	accepted for compatibility: the router always queues the review for the daemon
  -branch string
    	pull request head branch (defaults to the pull request's branch)
  -campaign string
    	campaign the review run is filed under
  -effort string
    	reasoning effort for runtimes that accept one
  -evidence-manifest string
    	absolute path of a JSON manifest (schema_version 1, head_sha, files[{path,bytes,sha256}]) of private files to install read-only into this remote E2B review's sandbox; every file is hash-verified now and again inside the sandbox; requires --exec-backend remote
  -exec-backend string
    	execution backend for this review: local or remote (default local)
  -exec-provider string
    	remote provider for this review: e2b (default), sandboxd or sandboxd-linux; a sandboxd provider implies --exec-backend remote and requires its [remote_exec.sandboxd] or [remote_exec.sandboxd-linux] section
  -full
    	review the full diff against the PR base even when a prior verdict at an ancestor head could bound the review
  -head string
    	exact 40-hex head to review (defaults to the pull request's current head)
  -head-sha string
    	same as --head
  -home string
    	home directory to use instead of the current user's home
  -json
    	print the request as JSON
  -message string
    	review instructions passed verbatim to the reviewer (same as a trailing positional)
  -model string
    	provider/model the review runs on, overriding the pool head
  -no-execution
    	review by reading code and the exact-head CI evidence only; the reviewer seat cannot run any program (omp, local backend, linux/amd64)
  -no-fix-target
    	accepted for compatibility and ignored: a review never routes a fix
  -org-role string
    	same as --role
  -part string
    	one part of a split review of the same head: a slug of letters, digits and dashes (e.g. mm-12-mm-15)
  -post-merge
    	review an already-merged head; findings become follow-ups instead of blocking a merge
  -pr int
    	pull request number
  -purpose string
    	review purpose: code, security, ui, or architecture (default "code")
  -reason string
    	why --supersede re-reviews the part; recorded on both runs
  -related-pr value
    	same-repository pull request whose exact head tree the reviewer gets read-only at .gitmoot-related/pr-N; repeatable; the daemon fetches refs/pull/N/head on this host and pins its head now
  -repo string
    	repository in owner/repo form (defaults to the current checkout)
  -reviewer string
    	registered reviewer to use instead of the router's choice
  -role string
    	requesting organization role notified with the verdict (defaults to GITMOOT_ORG_ROLE)
  -runtime string
    	override the runtime this review dispatches on (default omp)
  -session string
    	runtime session the review reuses
  -supersede string
    	re-review at the same head: the settled blocking review (of this --part, or the whole-head review without --part) whose verdict this request replaces once it lands; requires --reason
  -ttl duration
    	how long the requester waits before the wait expires to its parent (default 12h0m0s)
```

## gitmoot reviewer

```text
Usage:
  gitmoot reviewer start <name> --runtime omp --repo owner/repo [--path .] [--model model] [--effort effort] [--start-daemon]
  gitmoot ask <reviewer> "question" [--repo owner/repo] [--background] [--model model] [--effort effort] [--campaign label] [--runtime rt] [--session ref] [--home path] [--json]
  --runtime omp|shell runs THIS run on the named runtime; the reviewer's registered default runtime is unchanged.
    The overridden run never resumes the reviewer's default-runtime session: it runs on a fresh session of the
    override runtime, or on --session <ref> (an explicit session id, or — required for shell — a command;
    "last" is rejected because it resumes whichever session is most recent).
    Model rule: --model with --runtime is interpreted for the OVERRIDE runtime; without --model the run uses the
    override runtime's default model (the reviewer's configured default model is never applied to another runtime).
    Effort rule: --effort with --runtime is interpreted for the OVERRIDE runtime; without --effort the run uses the
    override runtime's default effort (the reviewer's configured default effort is never applied to another runtime).
  gitmoot reviewer type list|show|set ...
  gitmoot reviewer subscribe <name> --runtime omp|shell --session <id|name|last|command> --role <role> [--repo owner/repo...] [--model model] [--effort effort] --capability <capability>
    Omp sessions may use a UUID or fresh:<suffix> — never last, because omp never resumes. Shell sessions are commands.
  gitmoot reviewer allow <name> --repo owner/repo
  gitmoot reviewer deny <name> --repo owner/repo
  gitmoot reviewer repos <name>
  gitmoot reviewer show <name> [--json]
  gitmoot reviewer policy <name> --policy auto|read-only|workspace-write|danger-full-access [--home path]
  gitmoot reviewer list
  gitmoot reviewer remove <name>
  gitmoot reviewer restart <name>      # abandon + replace the runtime session (finish in-flight asks first)
  gitmoot reviewer doctor <name>
```

## gitmoot runtime

```text
Usage:
  gitmoot runtime list [--json]
  gitmoot runtime prune [--dry-run] [--min-idle 168h] [--json]

list shows the resolved metadata for each built-in runtime: capabilities, default
model/effort, known models, and where token usage is read from. Values come from the
compiled built-in defaults, overlaid with any [runtimes.<name>] config overrides.

prune removes staged runtime copies under <home>/runtimes that no job staged for
--min-idle and no live process uses. The daemon runs it daily with the default.
A removed copy is staged again the next time a job needs it.
```

## gitmoot runtime list

```text
Usage of runtime list:
  -home string
    	home directory to use instead of the current user's home
  -json
    	print the runtimes as a JSON array instead of the text table
```

## gitmoot runtime prune

```text
Usage of runtime prune:
  -dry-run
    	report what would be removed without removing anything
  -home string
    	home directory to use instead of the current user's home
  -json
    	print the report as JSON
  -min-idle duration
    	remove only copies no job staged for at least this long (default 168h0m0s)
```

## gitmoot sandbox

```text
Usage:
  gitmoot sandbox probe

probe reports whether this kernel enforces the runtime sandbox (Landlock):
it prints "supported (Landlock ABI vN)" and exits 0, or "unsupported"
and the reason and exits 1.
```

## gitmoot workflow

```text
External-coordinator workflow groups and journal.

Usage:
  gitmoot workflow list [--json]
  gitmoot workflow show-note <id> [--json]
  gitmoot workflow show <label> [--json] [--limit N]
  gitmoot workflow describe <label> "<text>" [--json]
  gitmoot workflow register <label> "<description>" [--json] [--home DIR]
  gitmoot workflow note <label> "<body>" [--author A] [--pane P] [--session ID] [--workdir PATH] [--no-auto] [--summary DESCRIPTION] [--status STATUS] [--repo owner/repo]
  gitmoot workflow close <label> [--reason R] [--json]
```
